Subject: Activation plan: pilot cascade + MAP (SOW attached)

Hi Olivia —

Congrats again on signing. Attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the SOW for the first phase. I sketched a condensed activation approach so your ops team can see the first 6 weeks at a glance:

- Week 0 (paperwork): finalize SOW, sign DocuSign (we noted the exceptions).
- Week 1 (prep): account provisioning, service account keys, network allow-lists, SOC2 checklist handoff.
- Week 2-3 (pilot canary): enable a 2-site pilot (North Clinic + Remote Teletriage) with reduced concurrency and dedicated logging.
- Week 4 (migration window): ramp traffic from staging -> production; cutover during 2-4am window.
- Week 5 (training): two half-day user sessions + admin workshop; asynchronous recordings posted.
- Week 6 (stabilize): KPI review and go/no-go for full roll.

Success criteria for pilot: 95th pctl latency <= 350ms for typical clinical prompts, zero data-plane errors > rate threshold, and acceptance tests passing in the eval harness.

Action items for Galaxy: share network CIDR and list of test patients; confirm pilot users (3 clinicians + 2 admins).

I also included a quick pilot checklist and the MAP spreadsheet in Drive (link below). Can we lock the pilot start for Monday, Dec 7? If that works I’ll schedule the training slots and book a canary run.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Short answer on rollback: we keep the staging cluster live as the immediate fallback. Operational steps:
1) Pause traffic at the ingress and restore routing to the staging endpoint (we keep a 5-minute warm standby).
2) If DNS is required, Redwood will coordinate a TTL-based rollback but Galaxy Ops must own the final DNS switch at their registrar.
3) We run the last known-good snapshot of model weights/config (we version in the MAP).

I can draft a one-page rollback runbook and include it in the MAP workbook.

- Dev
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
